**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-methods.html#/part-3-reproduce-then-take-the-model-apart){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).

Part 3 begins with the reproduction of one of three recorded results, chosen by you. The three reproduced models are three estimators, and they lead into what a panel of 27 countries needs from its methods: fixed effects against random intercepts, the within–between model, and a test that copes with few clusters. Then the menu is taken apart decision by decision, and the part ends with a round of exploration of your own.

| Analyst | Data | Model | Recorded by Multi100 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C6HJR | the course panel, `EUframes_cy.csv`, 270 country-years | fixed effects for country and year, conventional standard errors | t = −3.804 on 233 df |
| KQXUE | `analyst_KQXUE.csv`, 270 country-years | a fixed effect for each country, conventional standard errors | t = −7.169 on 242 df |
| 018OL | `analyst_018OL.csv`, 420 cells of country, year and wave | random intercepts for country, year and wave, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom | t = −1.206 on 396.9 df |

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the constrained task | The four instructions of the second Multi100 task, read verbatim, what each assumes, the columns of the panel, and the three analyses that can be reproduced on aggregate data. | 10 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) Task 3, or the working script | Choose one analyst and fill the gaps in its cell. The first run of the cell of 018OL downloads two packages, about 32 MB. Type the analyst and the value in the chat, for example `018OL t = -1.206`, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go. | 18 minutes |
| Slides, the three reproduced models and few clusters, with [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd), sections 3 to 5, as the companion | Why everyone with the same analyst got the same t and the three analysts did not; two-way and country fixed effects against random intercepts; the within–between model; conventional, clustered and CR2 errors with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom on the same estimate. | 12 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd) and slides | The fourteen decisions, the three levels into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps, what Task 2 of Multi100 left open, the ground rules for the menu and the claim-alignment convention. Every decision starts from the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR. | 10 minutes |
| Slides, the methodological tutorial | Nine of the fourteen decisions, a slide or two each: the six framing scales; building a scale from a mean, sum or share; claim alignment; a bounded scale in a linear model; the predictor; its form; the estimators for countries and years, and what fixed effects adjust for; the copredictor; sample restrictions; weights; making the axes comparable. | 22 minutes |
| Task 4 in the [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore) or the workspace, then [Multiverse](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd) | Call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, print them with `my_experiments()`, then submit the one you would defend with `submit_exploration()`. Your dot is drawn on the class chart as an exploratory result. | 18 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you have reproduced a recorded result, you can say what fixed effects, random intercepts and the CR2 test each do on this panel and what each decision of the menu does to an estimate, and you have an exploratory dot on the class chart.
